title: Finite restricted determinant tests give all degrees and scalar extensions
statement: Let $A$ be a commutative ring and $L$ a field in the same universe. Let $\alpha:\operatorname{Fin}(s)\to\mathbf N^n$ be an ordered vertex family for $D$ [def-trf-supported-homogeneous-division], $c_{i\gamma}\in A$, and $B:\mathbf N\to\mathbf N$. Suppose that for every $q\in\mathbf N$ and every commutative ring $R$ in that universe, $B(q)$ is a finite division test for the essential restriction of the $q$-prefix. Let $e:A\to L$ be a ring map. For the restricted forms $h_{i,q}$ and matrices $M_{q,t}$ of [def-trf-coefficient-division-data], assume $e(\det M_{q,t})\ne0$ whenever $q\le d_{\max}$ and $t\le B(q)$, where $d_{\max}=\max(\{0\}\cup\{|\alpha_i|\}_i)$. Then the mapped forms $e_*(h_{i,q})$ have unique supported homogeneous division in every prefix $q$ and every degree $t$. Moreover the forms $(j\circ e)_*(h_{i,q})$ have the same property for every field extension $j:L\to K$, with $K$ in any universe.

source.place: Bierstone--Milman, Invent. Math. 128 (1997), Lemma 7.7 pp.263--264, Theorem 8.1 pp.273--275, and completion of Theorem 9.6 p.282. BM read online at https://mahalex.net/teaching/seminars/gabber/Bierstone-Milman%20Canonical%20desingularization%20in%20characteristic%20zero.pdf; ILO VIII 2.3.11--2.3.13 is the route reference.

proof.text: The first-dividing-vertex bijection identifies the supported family with the degree-t monomial basis, making its regular coefficient matrix square. Every restricted form is homogeneous of the retained vertex degree. Under ev, nonzero determinant implies a basis and hence spanning in each tested degree.

source.place: Bierstone--Milman, Invent. Math. 128 (1997), Lemma 7.7 pp.263--264, Theorem 8.1 pp.273--275, and completion of Theorem 9.6 p.282. proof.text: Apply the finite-test equivalence in the supplied hypothesis for each prefix at most the maximum vertex degree. It upgrades spanning in the bounded degrees to unique division in all degrees. Above that maximum, both prefixes retain every vertex; their subtype indices, essential variable sets and coefficient sums identify with those at the maximum.

proof.text: In every degree, map the resulting square coefficient matrix and its inverse through j. Their inverse identities are preserved, so the coefficientwise mapped family is a basis over K. Coefficient maps commute with the finite monomial sums defining the restricted forms. This uses no new stabilization bound over K.
